title: Chapter 88 — Campaigns, Events & The Retail Calendar
intro: The promo calendar mastered, the event playbook, and quiet-season craft.

sections.title: The Seasonal Rhythm
sections.content:
January-February: post-holiday slowdown. Hit your builder pipeline. Follow up on every open quote from the holidays. Tax refund season starts mid-February — have financing promotions ready.

March-April: spring renovation kicks off. Kitchen packages. Tax refund money arrives. This is when homeowners start the projects they planned over winter.

May — Victoria Day and Memorial Day: major promotional weekend, one of the top three selling weekends. Pre-sell the week before — call every open quote and tell them the promotion is coming.

June-July: outdoor living season. BBQ and outdoor kitchen sales peak. Condo move-in season drives compact appliance demand.

August-September: laundry picks up with back-to-school. Labour Day is another top promotional weekend. Kitchen renovations push to complete before Thanksgiving.

October: renovation completion push — urgency is real. 'If we order today, you will have your new kitchen for the holidays.'

November — Black Friday: biggest single sales period, compressed margins. Volume matters more than margin.

December: year-end builder close-outs and gift purchases.

The best reps plan 30 days ahead. They know what promotion is coming and they ride the wave instead of being surprised by it.

sections.title: Event Selling
sections.content:
VIP shopping events, cooking demos, designer evenings — these are pipeline accelerators. An invite-only event makes customers feel special and creates urgency. In-person demos convert better than any advertisement.

The event playbook: curate the guest list from your CRM — invite open quotes, past customers due for replacement, and new prospects. Send personal invitations by phone or text, not mass email. Offer event-only pricing or exclusive previews. Have your design consultant and manufacturer reps available. Follow up with everyone who attended within 48 hours.

A well-run event with 30 attendees should produce 8-12 appointments and 4-6 sales within 30 days. That is a better ROI than any marketing spend.

sections.title: Quiet Season Craft
sections.content:
The slow months — January, February, July — are not down time. They are building time. This is when you invest in the pipeline that pays you during peak season.

Train on new products. The manufacturer just launched a new refrigerator line — learn it now so you are the expert when customers start shopping in March. Prospect new builder accounts. Clean your CRM — update contact info, move stale deals, tag follow-up priorities. Attend manufacturer training events. Build your social media content library.

Every rep who coasts in January and February scrambles in May. Every rep who prospects in January has a full pipeline when the promotions hit. The quiet season is where careers are built — not on the busy Saturday when everyone sells.
